variants: H1 and H1-2 on the product page, which lists user-development computing for both.
availability_note: Unitree's shop lists the H1 with an add-to-cart button. Buyers who want product information are told to contact Unitree directly.

hardware.compute: A standard configuration of an Intel Core i5 for platform functions and an Intel Core i7 for user development, with optional modules such as Orin NX.
hardware.sensors: 3D LiDAR plus a depth camera, which Unitree says gives 360-degree depth perception.
hardware.actuation: Low-inertia high-speed internal-rotor permanent magnet synchronous motors on industrial-grade crossed roller bearings. The H1 stands about 180 cm, weighs about 47 kg, and moves at 3.3 m/s with five degrees of freedom per leg and four expandable degrees per arm. The H1-2 stands about 178 cm, weighs about 70 kg, and has 27 degrees of freedom in total, with shoulder and elbow joints of about 120 N·m, wrists of about 30 N·m, and a rated arm load of about 7 kg.
hardware.power: A quickly replaceable 15 Ah (0.864 kWh) battery at up to 67.2 V.

developer_access: Unitree's unitree_rl_gym repository documents training a reinforcement-learning policy in simulation and deploying it to a physical H1 or H1-2 for motion control, and its unitree_ros2 repository documents controlling the H1 directly with ROS 2 messages, without wrapping the SDK interface.
terms_note: Unitree's SDK, unitree_sdk2, is released under the BSD 3-Clause License. Unitree's terms page has Terms, After-sales Terms, Privacy Policy, Disclaimer, and End User License Agreement tabs; the after-sales tab is the hardware warranty policy, and it excludes damage caused by the user's own developer-mode programs from free warranty. The H1 product page states no warranty period.
not_verified: The documented policy interfaces are Unitree's own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is a Unitree web page or repository file that Unitree can change at any time.
